title: The 10 Best Cordless Drills
subtitle: Ranked from live Amazon data — best-sellers, real ratings, honest trade-offs.
intro: We pulled the best-selling cordless drills on Amazon, then scored each one on a single 100-point scale built from its star rating, how many people have reviewed it, its value for the price, and its feature set. Two batteries or one, brushless or brushed, heavy-duty or grab-and-go — here is where each lands.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

avoid.name: JH Steady 21V Cordless Drill Driver Kit
avoid.flag: Listing contradicts itself on core specs
avoid.verdict: The lowest-ranked drill we found — and the listing itself is the reason. Skip it.
reasons: The spec sheet claims a 30,000 rpm max speed while the description says 1,500 rpm. A drill does not spin at 30,000 rpm — that is a rotary-tool number. When a listing contradicts itself on the headline spec, you can't trust anything else on the page.
"JH Steady" is a no-name brand with no service record, and the battery is a proprietary 21V pack. When it dies you are buying a whole new drill, not a replacement battery.
The page sells several different "kit options" under one listing, so its ratings may not even be for this exact drill — you can't tell what the stars are actually rating.
"21V" is marketing inflation. Serious drills run 18V or 20V MAX; padding the number to 21 is a spec game, not extra power.

buyers_guide.a: 12V drills are lighter and cheaper and handle furniture, shelves, and small jobs. 20V drills have the torque for drilling into hardwood, driving long screws, and general home projects. If you only own one drill, buy 20V.

Brushless motors run cooler, last longer, and squeeze more runtime from a battery. They cost more. For occasional DIY, a brushed drill like the DCD771 is fine; if you'll use it weekly, pay up for brushless.

buyers_guide.q: How much torque do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Torque is twisting power. Under ~300 in-lbs (or ~35 Nm) is light-duty — screws and small bits. Name-brand 20V drills push well past that for drilling into wood and metal. None of these are rated for concrete or masonry.
Two batteries mean you never stop to charge. Kits like the DCD771 and PULITUO include a spare; most budget drills ship with one, so factor a second battery into the price.
The chuck holds the bit. A 3/8 in chuck fits most home bits; a 1/2 in chuck accepts larger bits and grips better for heavy drilling. Keyless chucks let you swap bits by hand.
